title: Effective Federal Funds Rate (DFF) — Daily Snapshot
summary: The Effective Federal Funds Rate (DFF) remained flat at 3.64% across the observation period from April 9-13, 2026. No change was recorded day-over-day from April 12 to April 13. This is a daily interest rate data point from FRED, not a policy announcement.
key_points: Rate held constant at 3.64% for all five trading days from April 9-13, 2026
Source is raw quantitative data from FRED database, not a policy statement or commentary
why_it_matters: The EFFR is the primary overnight lending rate benchmark in the U.S. banking system. A flat reading at 3.64% indicates no interbank lending rate volatility and suggests the Federal Reserve's current policy rate is stable. However, this data snapshot alone does not convey policy intent or forward guidance.
macro_context: The stable EFFR at 3.64% reflects the Fed's current target rate environment. Without accompanying FOMC communications, this snapshot cannot be placed in a rate path context. The consistency over multiple days suggests market stability in overnight funding markets.
market_structure_context: The effective Fed funds rate is a volume-weighted average of overnight repo transactions among depository institutions. Flat readings across multiple days indicate orderly functioning in the fed funds market with no unusual pressure points.
